current_price_source: Yahoo Finance live fetch (query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/DELL) as of 2026-06-27; regularMarketPrice = 399.49

inputs.shares_note: Q1 FY2027 diluted share count (most recent, 3M ended May 1 2026). Down from 684M at FY2026 year-end due to ongoing buybacks.
inputs.net_debt_note: Net debt = TotalDebt ($31,503M) - Cash ($11,528M) = $19,975M. From FY2026 annual balance sheet (Jan 30 2026). Dell carries negative shareholders equity ($-2,470M) due to leveraged EMC acquisition history and heavy buybacks; equity-based valuation is inapplicable.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026 actual free cash flow ($8,552M = OCF $11,185M - CapEx $2,633M). This is a clean, reliable base; the previous model used a normalized $5,500M due to FY2025 FCF depression ($1,869M). FY2026 marks a full normalization. Q1 FY2027 FCF of $3,118M annualizes to ~$12.5B, confirming the recovery.

historical_growth.revenue_3yr_note: FY2023 ($102,301M) to FY2026 ($113,538M) = 3.5% CAGR. Suppressed by FY2024 PC market contraction (-14% YoY) and post-spinoff mix normalization.
historical_growth.revenue_5yr_note: FY2022 ($101,197M, first post-VMware year) to FY2026 ($113,538M) = 2.9% CAGR over 4 clean post-spinoff years. '5yr' label used for UI consistency; actual comparable span is 4 years.
historical_growth.eps_3yr_note: FY2023 GAAP EPS $3.24 to FY2026 $8.68 = 38.9% CAGR. Elevated by FY2023 being a depressed base (post-spinoff restructuring charges) and by FY2026 record earnings.
historical_growth.eps_5yr_note: FY2022 GAAP EPS $7.02 to FY2026 $8.68 = 5.4% CAGR over 4 years. More representative of underlying GAAP earnings power trajectory.
historical_growth.equity_cagr_note: Dell has had negative shareholders equity in every year since the 2016 EMC leveraged acquisition. Equity deficit at FY2026: -$2,470M. Equity CAGR cannot be calculated and has been excluded from the growth rate selection process. FCF-based DCF is the only applicable intrinsic value methodology.
historical_growth.fcf_3yr_note: FY2023 FCF ($562M, severely depressed by post-spinoff CapEx spike) to FY2026 FCF ($8,552M) = 147.8% CAGR. Statistically meaningless due to the distorted base year.
historical_growth.fcf_5yr_note: FY2024 FCF ($5,920M) to FY2026 FCF ($8,552M) = 20.2% CAGR over 2 years. The most reliable FCF CAGR available given the spinoff and AI-driven working capital distortions in adjacent years.
historical_growth.growth_rate_rationale: Year 1 (FY2027) growth rate of 47% anchored directly to Dell's raised management guidance of $165-169B revenue (midpoint $167B) vs FY2026 base of $113,538M. Historical revenue CAGRs (2.9-3.5%) are structurally distorted by the VMware spinoff and are completely irrelevant to the current AI-infrastructure supercycle inflection. Q1 FY2027 actual revenue of $43.8B (+88% YoY) with $51.3B AI backlog and $60B FY2027 AI server guidance provide exceptional near-term visibility. Growth decelerates materially in Years 2-5 as the AI capex cycle matures.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EQUITY CAGR UNUSABLE: Dell has sustained negative shareholders equity since the 2016 EMC leveraged acquisition (-$2,470M deficit at FY2026 year-end). Traditional equity/book-value growth metrics cannot be applied. FCF CAGRs are distorted by VMware spinoff timing (FY2022-FY2023), post-spinoff CapEx spike (FY2023), and AI server working capital consumption (FY2025). Only FY2026 FCF of $8,552M and the FY2027 forward guidance trajectory are reliable anchors for this DCF.
historical_growth.historical_fcf_note: FY2022: $7,511M | FY2023: $562M (post-spinoff CapEx spike) | FY2024: $5,920M | FY2025: $1,869M (AI server inventory/AR build) | FY2026: $8,552M (normalized, confirmed by Q1 FY2027 FCF of $3,118M). Q1 FY2027 annualizes to ~$12.5B, consistent with improving FCF trajectory.

valuation_philosophy: Dell's equity deficit renders book-value and equity-growth based valuation inapplicable. This model uses a forward-revenue-anchored FCF-DCF methodology, with Year 1 growth calibrated to management guidance and subsequent years incorporating reasonable deceleration scenarios. FCF margins (5.5% base, 6.5% bull, 4.0% bear) are set below the FY2026 actual 7.5% FCF margin to conservatively account for sustained gross margin compression from AI server mix (gross margin has compressed from ~24% to ~18% over the past year). The bull case FCF margin of 6.5% would require either margin recovery on AI servers as mix shifts toward enterprise/sovereign customers, or the AI supercycle producing operating leverage sufficient to offset the GPU hardware pass-through compression. The bear case acknowledges the risk that $60B of AI server revenue is structurally low-margin, with hyperscaler AI capex volatility threatening sustained FCF generation.

base.narrative: Year 1 growth anchored to management FY2027 guidance midpoint ($167B, +47% YoY). Growth decelerates as AI infrastructure cycle matures: Y2 reflects continued AI server shipments against the $51.3B backlog; Y3-Y5 incorporate normalization as enterprise deployments slow and PC refresh cycle winds down. FCF margin of 5.5% is below FY2026 actual 7.5% to reflect sustained AI mix gross margin compression (non-GAAP gross margin fell from 21.6% to 18.1% in Q1 FY2027). WACC of 10% reflects Dell's investment-grade credit profile, meaningful leverage (net debt $20B), cyclical hardware exposure, and prevailing interest rates. Terminal growth 3% = long-run nominal GDP growth rate.

bull.narrative: Year 1 beats guidance at $175B (top of $165-169B range plus Q1 FY2027 run-rate extrapolation). Strong compounding driven by: (1) AI backlog conversion accelerating as supply constraints ease in H1 FY2028; (2) agentic AI creating incremental traditional server demand beyond GPU servers; (3) CSG commercial revenue sustaining growth as AI PCs drive ASP expansion; (4) sovereign AI and Pentagon CETA contract scaling into meaningful revenue contributors. FCF margin improves to 6.5% as enterprise/sovereign AI server mix carries better pricing than hyperscaler direct deals, and services attach rates improve. Lower WACC reflects reduced credit risk as net debt declines toward $10B. Terminal growth 3.5% captures AI-enabled services revenue streams becoming recurring.

bear.narrative: Year 1 revenue below guidance at $140B as: (1) supply constraints (DRAM, NAND, CPU, HDD) cause AI backlog pushouts from H2 FY2027 into FY2028; (2) hyperscaler AI capex moderates following extraordinary Q1 FY2027 demand; (3) tariff impacts add margin pressure not fully passed through. Growth slows sharply to 2-6% as the AI server super-cycle peaks earlier than expected and the Windows refresh cycle completes. FCF margin of 4.0% reflects structural compression: high GPU component pass-through (NVIDIA captures most value chain economics), component inflation, and elevated interest expense from remaining debt. Higher WACC (12%) reflects execution risk and credit quality concerns if FCF weakens. Terminal growth 2% = sustained commodity hardware producer with limited pricing power.

base.note: Entry price to achieve 15% CAGR = intrinsic value ($232.40) / (1.15^5). At $399.49, the stock would need to compound at ~-10.2% annually to reach base IV, or base IV must prove understated.

bull.note: Entry price to achieve 15% CAGR = bull IV ($424.27) / (1.15^5). Even in the bull case, 15% CAGR entry would require a $211 entry point; current $400 price achieves ~1.2% CAGR to bull IV.

bear.note: Bear scenario is catastrophic from current levels. Risk asymmetry is highly unfavorable: base downside -42%, bear downside -85%, versus bull upside of only +6%.

sensitivity.note: Base case WACC=10%, Terminal Growth=3% (highlighted cell). Matrix shows intrinsic value per share using base case FCF projections (5.5% FCF margin on guided revenue path). Net debt $19,975M subtracted; shares 656M. Current price $399.49 is only exceeded in the WACC=8%, terminal growth 4% scenario ($418.93). The market price requires either aggressive WACC assumptions or higher FCF margins than the 5.5% base case.

probability_weighted.note: Weighted IV = (0.25 x $424.27) + (0.50 x $232.40) + (0.25 x $59.07) = $106.07 + $116.20 + $14.77 = $237.04. Implies approximately -40.7% downside from current $399.49. The market is pricing a scenario more aggressive than our base case, likely reflecting: (1) greater confidence in AI supercycle duration; (2) FCF margin improvement expectations above 5.5%; or (3) multiple expansion beyond what the DCF captures for an AI infrastructure leader.

p_fy2027_gaap_eps.note: 23.1x FY2027 guided GAAP EPS of $17.31 is reasonable for a company with 99% YoY GAAP EPS growth. Within normal range for high-growth technology hardware.

p_fy2027_nongaap_eps.note: 22.3x FY2027 guided non-GAAP EPS of $17.90. Not stretched given the growth trajectory.

ev_fy2027_ebit.note: 21.1x forward EV/EBIT is justified for a company growing EBIT by ~65% YoY with a record $51.3B backlog.

p_fy2027_fcf.note: 26.2x forward P/FCF is not obviously excessive for a company with this growth trajectory. FY2026 FCF margin was 7.5%; 6% is conservative.

ev_revenue.note: EV/Revenue of 2.5x on trailing FY2026 revenue is reasonable for a hardware company. On FY2027 guided revenue ($167B), EV/Revenue = 1.69x - extremely low for any tech company.

dcf_gap_check.note: Base case DCF IV of $232.40 is -41.8% below current price of $399.49, exceeding the -30% divergence threshold. This means the current price requires bull-case or better assumptions to be supported by discounted cash flows.

market_implied_fcf_margin.note: To justify $399.49 with WACC=10% and TG=3%, the model requires ~8% FCF margin on the guided revenue path - above FY2026 actual 7.5%. With WACC=9% and TG=3.5%, a 7.5% FCF margin yields ~$420 IV. The market appears to be pricing: (a) FCF margins recovering toward historical 7%+ levels, AND (b) a modestly lower WACC reflecting Dell's strong cash generation and government contract visibility.

sanity_check.overall_assessment: Multiple-based valuation checks PASS (P/E 23x, EV/EBIT 21x, P/FCF 26x are not stretched for the growth profile). The DCF base case TRIPS the divergence threshold because the base conservatively uses 5.5% FCF margins vs FY2026 actual 7.5% and Q1 FY2027 annualized margin of ~7.1%. The market is pricing continued FCF margin near 7%+ and a slightly lower WACC (9%), which is a defensible assumption given: Q1 FY2027 beat guidance by $8.1B; $51.3B AI backlog; 74% guided EPS growth; and the $9.7B Pentagon CETA contract. The stock is NOT a screaming buy by DCF at current prices (requires near-bull assumptions), but is not obviously egregiously overvalued by traditional multiples. Margin of safety is thin.

warning_banner.message: Current price ($399.49) requires bull-case assumptions to be supported by DCF. Base case intrinsic value is $232 (-42%). Market multiples (P/E 23x, EV/EBIT 21x) are not stretched for the growth trajectory, but the DCF margin of safety is negative at current price. Only the bull scenario ($424) implies meaningful upside. Key risk: AI server FCF margins staying compressed at 4-5% would make current price difficult to justify.

analyst_notes.key_consideration_1: The Q1 FY2027 quarter ($43.8B revenue, +88% YoY) was so extraordinary that it has fundamentally re-rated Dell from a cyclical hardware company to an AI infrastructure leader. AI server revenue of $16.1B in a single quarter, a $51.3B backlog, and FY2027 guidance raised by $27B in one announcement are historically unprecedented for a company of this scale. The market's re-rating from $117 (February 2026) to $400 (June 2026) reflects this fundamental repositioning - the stock has tripled in less than 5 months.
analyst_notes.key_consideration_2: Net debt of $19.975B at $656M shares outstanding means approximately $30.45 per share of debt overhang. In the base case, this reduces equity value from a $263/share enterprise value to $232/share IV. Rapid FCF generation ($8.5B in FY2026, $12.5B annualized in Q1 FY2027) means net debt is declining materially, which is a positive catalyst not fully captured in the static balance sheet snapshot.
analyst_notes.key_consideration_3: FCF margin is the critical uncertainty. FY2026 actual FCF margin was 7.5%. Q1 FY2027 FCF margin was 7.1%. The base case conservatively assumes 5.5%, the bull case 6.5%, and the bear 4%. If Dell sustains 7%+ FCF margins on $167B of FY2027 revenue, base case IV would be approximately $328-389 (WACC 9-10%), much closer to current prices. The FCF margin outlook hinges on whether AI server mix continues to compress gross margins or stabilizes as enterprise/sovereign mix grows.
analyst_notes.key_consideration_4: The probability-weighted IV of $237 implies -41% downside, but the distribution of outcomes is extremely wide: bull +6%, bear -85%. This fat-tail risk profile is characteristic of a company at the center of a potential technology supercycle. The key investor question is whether the AI infrastructure buildout is a durable multi-year secular trend or a cyclical peak. Management's commentary ('pipelines have never been healthier', agentic AI as a new demand wave) and the 50%+ growth in active AI customers to 5,000+ suggest durability, but history shows technology hardware cycles can reverse sharply.
analyst_notes.key_consideration_5: The $9.7B DoD CETA contract (five-year blanket purchase agreement) announced May 2026 is a significant quality signal. Government contracts provide durable revenue floors, reduce cyclicality, and signal Dell's trusted status in the highest-security federal environments. Long-duration government revenue streams deserve a lower WACC discount than pure commercial hardware revenue - the bull case WACC of 9% partially reflects this.
analyst_notes.key_consideration_6: Dell's stock has appreciated approximately 242% in the 4 months since the February 2026 FY2026 earnings report. At $399.49, the market has priced in most of the near-term AI supercycle upside. From a risk/reward perspective, the asymmetry has shifted substantially: the base case DCF implies -42% downside, the bull case only +6% upside. Investors buying at $400 are making a concentrated bet on the bull scenario materializing and FCF margins remaining above 6.5%. This is a fundamentally different risk profile than the $117 price point where the previous DCF was built.
analyst_notes.key_consideration_7: Supply constraints cited by management (DRAM, NAND, CPUs, HDDs) for H2 FY2027 are actually a demand signal - they indicate backlog is real and orders are firm. However, they also mean Q2-Q4 FY2027 revenue could disappoint vs. the run-rate implied by Q1 FY2027, creating potential short-term stock volatility even if the long-term thesis is intact. Watch for Q2 FY2027 earnings (guided $44-45B revenue) as the next major inflection point.
analyst_notes.previous_model_comparison: Previous DCF (Feb 2026, price $117): Base IV $129, weighted IV $130, implied +11% upside. Current model (Jun 2026, price $400): Base IV $232, weighted IV $237, implied -41% downside. The 242% stock price increase dramatically outpaced the improvement in intrinsic value, which has grown ~80% in the same period (from normalized $5.5B FCF base to $8.5B+ actual with improving trajectory). The valuation re-rating from value to growth premium accounts for the gap.
